1.pericope_label: Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land
debates: Why a new discourse begins at this point
What kind of controversy is meant
Which of the three missing things is the root
outliers: Calvin voices the objection that a God who threatens after promising must be changeable, and answers it from the way men are taught
Ellicott would replace mercy with love, on the ground that one Hebrew word covers both the covenant love of God and its answer in man
themes: A promise yesterday and a summons today
A court where the plaintiff is also the judge
Charges that lie only against a covenant people
Honesty gone before knowledge of God is missed

2.pericope_label: By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood. Therefore shall the land mourn, and every one that dwelleth therein shall languish, with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of heaven; yea, the fishes of the sea also shall be taken away
debates: What the first word in the list means
Who the thieves and murderers are
Why the animals share the judgment
outliers: Calvin insists the thieves and murderers named are the honoured and wealthy, the only illustrious men in the nation
Clarke accounts for the loss of the fish by shoals turned away from the coast, a thing he says has often happened
themes: A charge read straight off the commandments
Blood reaching blood without a break
A land mourning for what its people did
Shoals that do not come to the coast that year

4.pericope_label: Yet let no man strive, nor reprove another: for thy people are as they that strive with the priest. Therefore shalt thou fall in the day, and the prophet also shall fall with thee in the night, and I will destroy thy mother
debates: Who is forbidding the reproof
What striving with the priest means
What the day and the night mark
outliers: Ellicott repoints the clause so that the priest is the person addressed and the people are called the adversaries of God
Clarke reports an old manuscript that omits the word priest altogether, leaving only that the people are rebels
themes: A nation that will not be told anything
A beam in the eye of every would-be reprover
Pupils who claim to know more than their teachers
A fall timed for the day of plenty

6.pericope_label: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children
debates: Which people are destroyed
Whether the priests or the people are the more to blame
Who is addressed in the singular
outliers: Ellicott offers a reading in which the people themselves lose a priesthood every member of the nation should have held
Gill excludes the elect from the threat before letting it fall on the nation
themes: A nation perishing of what it refused to learn
Teachers who taught as if they had not taught
Darkness drawn round a man for an excuse
The honour of an office without the office

7.pericope_label: As they were increased, so they sinned against me: therefore will I change their glory into shame. They eat up the sin of my people, and they set their heart on their iniquity
debates: What it was that increased
Whose glory is turned into shame
Whether the sin eaten is the offering or the offence
outliers: Calvin rejects the sin-offering rendering outright, holding that it destroys the point, which is that the priests lived off the superstition of the people
Keil and Delitzsch have the priests wishing the sins of the people to multiply so that more sacrificial meat would come to them
themes: A nation that credited its idols for its harvests
A well-fed horse kicking at its master
Glory already traded for the likeness of an ox
Men who profit by the sins they should remove

9.pericope_label: And there shall be, like people, like priest: and I will punish them for their ways, and reward them their doings. For they shall eat, and not have enough: they shall commit whoredom, and shall not increase: because they have left off to take heed to the Lord
debates: Whether the threat falls on the priest or on the people
Why eating fails to satisfy
What the barrenness threatened is
outliers: Calvin denies that the levelling of priest and people exhausts the threat, since God vindicates his law against other sinners too
Keil and Delitzsch divide the verse clause by clause between the priests and the whole nation
themes: A congregation that wanted its teachers mute
Booty gathered from every quarter and worth nothing
Bread that does not feed the man who eats it
Licence that produces no children

11.pericope_label: Whoredom and wine and new wine take away the heart. My people ask counsel at their stocks, and their staff declareth unto them: for the spirit of whoredoms hath caused them to err, and they have gone a whoring from under their God
debates: What it is that takes away the heart
Why the people are still called the people of God
What the staff that answers them was
outliers: Calvin denies that the opening sentence is the general proverb most take it for, and confines it to one prosperous nation
Ellicott allows that the staff may be the idol itself rather than a divining rod, on the strength of a goddess worshipped in that form
themes: Plenty that leaves no particle of understanding
A chosen name kept only to sharpen the charge
Counsel asked of a trunk that was once a tree
A blind man questioning his own stick

13.pericope_label: They sacrifice upon the tops of the mountains, and burn incense upon the hills, under oaks and poplars and elms, because the shadow thereof is good: therefore your daughters shall commit whoredom, and your spouses shall commit adultery. I will not punish your daughters when they commit whoredom, nor your spouses when they commit adultery
debates: What the fornication charged earlier actually was
Why the women are left unpunished
What the separation in the last clause means
outliers: Calvin takes the separation as separation from God rather than of husbands from wives, and says the literal reading misses the reason given
Keil and Delitzsch hear God turn away from the nation at mid-verse and begin speaking of it in the third person
themes: Worship offered on the highest ground available
Sincere zeal that is still called adultery
Judgment withheld as the worst judgment of all
A shade chosen for what it hides

15.pericope_label: Though thou, Israel, play the harlot, yet let not Judah offend; and come not ye unto Gilgal, neither go ye up to Beth-aven, nor swear, The Lord liveth
debates: Which kingdom the warning is addressed to
Which of the places called Gilgal is meant
Why swearing by the name is forbidden here
outliers: Ellicott reports a Greek manuscript that reads the name of the Egyptian city of sun-worship in place of the altered name of Bethel
Gill offers a second reading in which the whole verse is addressed to Israel, warning them not to draw Judah into their own sins
themes: A neighbour whose disease is catching
A house of God renamed a house of vanity
A camp of the conquest turned into a shrine
An oath that must not be mixed with the wrong worship

16.pericope_label: For Israel slideth back as a backsliding heifer: now the Lord will feed them as a lamb in a large place. Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone
debates: What the figure of the heifer means
Whether the lamb in a large place is mercy or judgment
Who is told to leave Ephraim alone
outliers: Ellicott reports a reading in which the lamb in a wide field is an expression of tender commiseration rather than a threat
Calvin takes the last words as God dismissing his own prophet from a commission that has failed
themes: A beast that slides back in the furrow
A wish granted as a punishment
A lamb bleating in a field too wide for it
A worker told to stop working

18.pericope_label: Their drink is sour: they have committed whoredom continually: her rulers with shame do love, Give ye. The wind hath bound her up in her wings, and they shall be ashamed because of their sacrifices
debates: What the sour drink means
What the rulers are said to have loved
Whether the wind binds the people or the people the wind
outliers: Keil and Delitzsch reject the conditional reading on the ground that intoxication leads to licentiousness and temperance does not
Calvin prefers the rendering in which the people bind the wind in their own wings, taking it for the vain confidence that makes men bold against God
themes: Drink gone flat and turned to vinegar
Shields that loved a bribe
Wind gathered into the skirt of a garment
Confidence that turns out to be the shame
